blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights Netflix's Chaos Automation Platform (ChAP), an automated system for running chaos engineering experiments in production to test system resilience under failure conditions. The paper emphasizes that such experiments are not fundamentally different from other production changes (e.g., bug fixes or A/B tests) and require careful monitoring and statistical analysis. ChAP evaluates system health under degraded conditions (e.g., service latency or failures) by routing a small percentage of user traffic to canary clusters with injected faults. Key components include fault injection (FIT), telemetry (Atlas, Mantis), and automated analysis (Kayenta). The authors also introduce Monocle, a dependency analysis tool that automatically generates targeted experiments by identifying service dependencies and vulnerabilities, such as misaligned timeouts or unsafe fallbacks. The system includes safeguards to limit blast radius, such as restricting experiments to business hours and capping traffic impact.
